ticket.title: storypole verify --summary fabricates a manual receipt with exit_code 0 instead of annotating the executed chain
ticket.description: Measured 2026-11-10 while verifying SP-24. lifecycle_cmds/mod.rs:159 builds the receipt override when args.verifier.is_some() OR args.summary.is_some(), and the record it builds is verifier manual with command n/a, exit_code Some(0), chain_key None and no commit window. So --summary, a flag whose documented purpose is to record what was verified, is an alias for a manual attestation: it does not annotate the executed chain, it replaces it with a claim that ran nothing. The failure is currently masked rather than absent, because refusal 2 (SP-40) fires whenever the task has a resolvable chain, which is how it surfaced: storypole verify SP-24 --summary was refused with the manual-receipt message even though --manual was never passed. In a repository whose config resolves no chain the same code path would write a receipt reading exit_code 0 after running nothing, which is precisely the failure GB-272 was filed to end. Wanted: --manual alone selects the attestation path; --summary and --verifier annotate the receipt the chain produced, so the command, exit code and chain key stay those of the run; and the attestation path keeps refusing when a chain exists. Acceptance: verify --summary on a task with a chain executes the chain and the receipt names it with the caller note attached, verify --manual without a chain still records an attestation, and a test pins that --summary alone never yields verifier manual.
